solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Round present nearly pops

parts.note: round in the sense of plump or stout

indicators.note: nearly means the word falls one letter short of complete, losing its tail

parts.note: present as in being here, at hand

explanation.surface: Someone presents a round of drinks and is close to bursting, or a balloon is about to pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims HERE to HER. 'pops' looks like a verb but is the informal name for a dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Pops is an informal, affectionate name for one's dad, the male parent.

clue.text: Livid at dropping new air freshener?

indicators.note: dropping means the letter is moved further down the word, in a down clue

parts.note: livid means furious, fuming

explanation.surface: Someone furious at having to give up their new air freshener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' moves the N of FUMINGAT lower down. The question mark admits a smoke for killing pests hardly freshens air.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a chemical released as smoke or vapour to disinfect a room, cleansing its air.

clue.text: Remove surveillance, not having succeeded

indicators.note: not having means the following letter is absent

parts.note: a stakeout is police surveillance of a place
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An order to end a surveillance operation that has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove something is to extract or take it away, a phrasal verb with the same sense.

clue.text: Competent, constant company has to quit

indicators.note: has to quit means the following letters leave the word

parts.note: a coefficient is a constant multiplier in algebra

explanation.surface: A capable employee, constantly with the firm, is forced to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constant' looks like an adjective describing the company but is a mathematical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A capable worker gets tasks done well with little waste, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Piece together with this means of suppressing report

definitions.text: Piece together with this means of suppressing report

parts.words: Piece together with this means of suppressing report
parts.note: piece is slang for a gun; fit this device to the gun and it muffles the bang, the report

explanation.surface: Instructions for assembling something that will hush up an embarrassing report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece together' looks like assembling a puzzle, and 'report' like a document; really a gun (piece) and its bang (report).
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's muffler is fitted onto the barrel to deaden the sound of firing.

clue.text: Inane flirt with rope exercising heavenly body

indicators.note: exercising means putting the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: A silly flirt working out with a rope, showing off their heavenly body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' suggests an attractive physique but here means a celestial one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury and Venus orbit closer to the Sun than Earth, which is the astronomer's term for them.

clue.text: Reportedly put away crew, perhaps

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than seen, matching by pronunciation

parts.note: to put away food is to have eaten it

explanation.surface: It is said that a crew was locked up, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' looks like jailing but means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew is an example: a racing boat holds this many oarsmen.

clue.text: Scientist, primarily medical, intending to cut body part

indicators.note: to cut means to go into, splitting the word

parts.note: the chest is part of the body

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A medical scientist plans to operate on part of a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives M and I, which go inside CHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is a practitioner of chemistry, one of the sciences.

clue.text: Internet exposed corrupt setter?

indicators.note: corrupt means the remaining letters are spoilt and rearranged
exposed means the word is stripped of its outer covering, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An internet leak reveals a dishonest crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips Internet to NTERNE and 'corrupt' rearranges it. 'setter?' is not a compiler but something that makes milk set.
explanation.definitionFit: This curdling agent makes milk set into curds for cheese.

clue.text: Literally aim for something rather rare

parts.note: read letter by letter, aim shows the Roman numeral I (one) placed in A, then M (a thousand)

explanation.surface: A target worth aiming for that is hard to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' asks for the letters of aim: I is Roman one, set in A followed by M, Roman for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a very rare person or thing, scarce enough to occur once among very many.

clue.text: Mock brand, one from Milan, checked by females

parts.note: a make is a brand of product

indicators.note: checked by means held in, stopped by the two letters on either side

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural
UNO is Italian for one, and Milan is in Italy

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a brand, perhaps one from Milan, while women keep them in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to ridicule or tease them, the same as this idiom.

clue.text: Who'd want energy reduced, loosely?

indicators.note: loosely means the remaining letters are not held in their order and are rearranged
reduced means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A question about who would like to see energy use cut, loosely speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the Y from ENERGY and 'loosely' rearranges ENERG. The whole clue also describes an environmentalist.
explanation.definitionFit: An environmentalist campaigner wants energy consumption cut, and is called by this colour as a noun.

clue.text: As some might say, disparage current dish

indicators.note: some people would pronounce the following words to sound just like the Italian dish

parts.note: to knock something is to criticise or disparage it; I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a dish that is currently in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As some might say' warns the sound match depends on pronunciation: KNOCK-I said aloud approximates the Italian word.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small Italian potato dumplings, served as a pasta-like course.

clue.text: On which you could get jolly high

definitions.text: On which you could get jolly high

parts.words: On which you could get jolly high
parts.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, who could climb this rope ladder up a ship's rigging

explanation.surface: Something that makes you very merry and elated, like a drink or drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' reads as 'very' but is naval slang for a Royal Marine; 'high' means up the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the small rope rungs tied across a ship's shrouds, forming a ladder aloft.

clue.text: A little disconcerting about what goes into bangers

indicators.note: about means the run of letters is turned round, read the other way
a little of the word means a few of its letters, found inside it

explanation.surface: Somewhat unsettling to learn what goes into sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ERTIN (from inside disconcerting) round. Bangers here are fireworks, not British sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a key ingredient of gunpowder used in fireworks.

clue.text: Renegade orphan regularly sent back by express

indicators.note: sent back means the picked letters are read in reverse
regularly means taking every other letter of the word, starting with the first

parts.note: to express something is to state it

explanation.surface: A rebellious orphan keeps being returned by express delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes OPA from orphan and 'sent back' turns it to APO.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade abandons their faith or cause, just as a defector from religion does.

clue.text: Mostly sensitive, kind secretary should do so

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: touchy means sensitive, easily offended
a type is a kind or sort

explanation.surface: Advice that a secretary should be mostly sensitive and kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts TOUCHY to TOUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A good secretary keys text without looking at the keys, which is this verb.

clue.text: Principle broken by workers in slum housing?

indicators.note: broken by means split apart with the other part inserted

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A principle that workers broke in slum housing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large block of flats, often run-down; the question mark admits it need not be a slum.

clue.text: Possibly returns to secure pine frame

indicators.note: to secure means to hold the next part safely inside
returns tells us the word is turned back to front

parts.note: possibly signals a definition by example: in golf, putts are shots, and puts are throws in shot-putting, so 'puts' is a possible sense
to pine or itch is to long for something

explanation.surface: Perhaps some returned goods are used to fix a wooden pine frame in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns PUTS into STUP, which then holds ITCH. 'Possibly' marks puts as one sense among several. 'frame' looks like a noun but is the verb: to incriminate falsely.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame someone is to set them up to take blame for something they didn't do.

clue.text: Coach briefly interrupting hackneyed testimonial

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the other word

parts.note: trite means hackneyed, overused

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A sports coach cuts into an unoriginal testimonial speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a trainer but means a bus; 'briefly' cuts it to BU.
explanation.definitionFit: A testimonial is an act or gift honouring someone, the same as this word.

clue.text: Loose relative forgoes introduction

indicators.note: forgoes introduction means the word gives up its opening letter

parts.note: an aunt or auntie is a family relative

explanation.surface: A wayward relative who skips the formal introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like an adjective describing the relative but is the verb: to unfasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or bond is to unfasten or undo it.

clue.text: Dissertations about universal hero

indicators.note: about means going around the other letter

parts.note: theses are dissertations
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: Dissertations about a hero who is universally admired.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero of myth slew the Minotaur in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Fly sheet he put out, repeatedly flapping

indicators.note: flapping suggests the letters moving about and changing order
repeatedly means the remainder is used twice
put out means the following letters are removed from the word

explanation.surface: A sheet that a man has put out on the line keeps flapping in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' drops HE from sheet to leave SET; 'repeatedly' doubles it and 'flapping' rearranges SETSET.
explanation.definitionFit: This African biting fly transmits sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Touchy-feely service upset enthusiasts at heart

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged
at heart means the inner core of the word, here with a few letters off each end

explanation.surface: Some hands-on service has disturbed enthusiasts deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' keeps THUSIAS from enthusiasts and 'upset' rearranges it. 'Touchy-feely' is used literally: a service delivered by touch.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese massage therapy applies finger pressure to points on the body.

clue.text: Foreign festival touring heart of tribal region

indicators.note: touring means going around the other part

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival

indicators.note: heart of means the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A festival abroad goes around the heart of a tribal region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes IB from tribal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan plateau is an autonomous region of China.

clue.text: Successfully conclude long drawn-out vote, welcoming Independent

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest inside

parts.note: to long for is to ache for something
I is the standard abbreviation for Independent, as in an election candidate

indicators.note: drawn-out means its inner letters are pulled out, leaving only the outer two

explanation.surface: A long, protracted vote finally concludes, with an independent candidate welcomed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn-out' leaves VE from vote, so ACHE plus VE holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something off or accomplish it is to reach a successful conclusion.

clue.text: Try to get free ride due to whiff in vacant taxicab

indicators.note: in means one part goes inside the other
vacant means the word is emptied of its contents, leaving only its ends

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell, a whiff

explanation.surface: Hitching a lift because there is a smell in an empty taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties taxicab to its two ends. Hum is British slang for a nasty smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhikers stick out a digit to beg a lift, so the verb means cadge a ride.

clue.text: Cool-temperature heavy fuel ultimately bearing flammable gas

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent, cool

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of each of the two words

parts.note: ENE, east-north-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A description of a heavy fuel that is kept cool, for some technical purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of heavy and fuel, giving Y and L.
explanation.definitionFit: This hydrocarbon gas burns very hot and is used in welding torches.

clue.text: Almost plan on result some time later?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding part

parts.note: an event can be an outcome or result

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short, dropping its last

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: An almost-settled plan that will only show results at some later date.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places one piece after another. The question mark is there because 'some time later' plays on late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: This poetic word means evening, a time late in the day.

clue.text: These are loaded in black frame

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a set can mean a frame or setting, as in a set of stones

explanation.surface: Riddle: these things are loaded inside a black frame, like bullets in a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' suggests ammunition but means very rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for wealthy, and fashionable rich travellers form this group.
